Stop Reporting Reach

Playbooklowob research

By lowob · 23 March 2026 · 6-minute read · Revenue

Pick the few numbers that show attention turning into money that comes back: activation, retention, revenue, efficiency and source. Instrument them before you spend on growth, report them to everyone who matters, and drop the vanity metrics from the top of the page. Reach is the easiest number to grow and the weakest evidence: a display impression counts as viewable when half the ad is on screen for one second, and in Keyrock's study of 62 airdrops in 2024, 88% of tokens lost value, most within 15 days.

The question every number has to answer

Did someone do something that makes the business more likely to exist next year? If a metric can rise while the answer is no, it belongs in an appendix.

Reach and impressions fail the test by construction. The industry standard for a viewable display impression, set by the Media Rating Council, is 50% of the ad's pixels on screen for one continuous second; for video, two seconds. That is a floor for counting exposure, not evidence anyone noticed. Follower counts and cumulative totals fail it too. Andreessen Horowitz's guide to startup metrics makes the point about cumulative charts: they always rise for any active business, so they can look healthy while the business shrinks. The same guide calls downloads "really just a vanity metric" and asks for cohort retention instead.

What to measure

StageWeb3AIWhy it matters
ActivationFirst deposit, first trade, first onchain actionFirst task completed, first integration liveInterest became use
RetentionDeposits and wallets still active at 30 / 90 daysWeekly active users or teams at 30 / 90 daysUse became habit
RevenueProtocol revenue, net of incentivesPaid accounts, net revenue retentionHabit became money
EfficiencyCost per retained depositor, incentive spend per $ of sticky TVLCustomer acquisition cost, payback periodMoney exceeds what it cost
SourceWhich partner, campaign or referral brought themSameWhere to spend next

Two definitions need care. "Active" means whatever the company decides it means, and the a16z guide warns that some definitions count accidental one-time users; write the definition down and keep it. And revenue is not the same as fees or bookings. DefiLlama, a widely used public DeFi dashboard, separates fees (everything users pay) from revenue (the subset the protocol keeps after paying liquidity providers) and lists incentives (tokens handed to users) as a separate line. Report revenue net of incentives. For AI and SaaS, our comparison of NRR and GRR covers which retention number to put first, and CAC payback covers efficiency.

The incentive adjustment

In web3, separate what you paid for from what you earned. Report TVL, volume and users both with and without incentivised activity. If 80% disappears when incentives end, the honest number is the 20%, and investors will compute it whether you do or not.

The evidence on airdrops shows why. Keyrock's analysis of 62 airdrops across several chains in 2024 found 88% of tokens declined in value, most within 15 days of distribution, and only 8 of the 62 showed positive returns after 90 days. Its successful cases had an existing user base, rewarded actual usage and released tokens in stages; one failure attracted reward hunters because it had little prior product traction. Activity bought with incentives behaves like rented activity. Our piece on community that survives the airdrop covers how to design for the people who stay.

The same principle applies to AI products running free tiers or heavy discounts. Report the paid and the free separately. Andreessen Horowitz makes the parallel point about acquisition cost: blended CAC, which counts organic customers, cannot show whether paid acquisition is profitable, so report paid CAC beside it.

If a metric can rise while the business is no more likely to exist next year, it belongs in an appendix.

Instrument before you spend

The most expensive mistake in early go-to-market is a year of activity with no way to tell what worked. Before spending meaningfully on any channel:

  1. Tag every link and referral by source.
  2. Track activation and 30-day retention by source, not just in aggregate.
  3. For web3, map wallet addresses to campaigns where you can do so properly and lawfully.
  4. Write down what result would make you double the channel and what would make you stop it.

The fourth step is the one most often skipped, and the one that turns reporting into decisions. Our piece on campaign testing that reaches a decision covers how to set those thresholds at low volumes.

One report, three audiences

The monthly report you send investors should contain the same core numbers your team runs the business on, and a version of it should be what you share with your community. Different detail, same truth. If the investor update and the internal dashboard disagree, one of them is wrong. Our piece on commercial KPIs a board will trust covers how to define each number once and reconcile it to finance.

AudienceDetailSame core numbers
TeamWeekly, by channel and cohortActivation, retention, revenue, efficiency, source
InvestorsMonthly, with trend and commentaryThe same five, incentivised and organic split
CommunityMonthly or quarterly, summarisedThe same five, without commercially sensitive detail

What to stop reporting

  • Impressions and reach, at the top of anything.
  • Follower counts as progress.
  • Waitlist size without a conversion rate.
  • Cumulative totals in place of monthly figures.
  • Incentivised volume without the unincentivised number next to it.
  • "Partnerships announced" without what each one produced.
Gateway card

The checklist

  • Five numbers: activation, retention, revenue, efficiency, source
  • A written definition of "active" and of revenue net of incentives
  • Incentivised and organic reported separately
  • Every channel tagged before money goes in
  • A double-or-stop rule for each channel
  • One monthly report, the same core numbers for every audience

lowob takeaways

  • Use one test for every number. If it can rise while the business is no more likely to exist next year, it belongs in an appendix.
  • Separate bought activity from earned. Most airdropped tokens lose value within weeks; report the unincentivised number.
  • Instrument before you spend. Tag every link and referral, and track activation and 30-day retention by source.
  • Send one truth to three audiences. Investors, the team and the community see the same core numbers at different levels of detail.

Common questions

What metrics should a startup report instead of reach and impressions?

Five numbers: activation, retention, revenue, efficiency and source. For web3 that means first deposit, active wallets at 30 and 90 days, protocol revenue net of incentives and cost per retained depositor; for AI, first task completed, weekly active teams, net revenue retention and payback.

How should a crypto project report TVL that includes incentives?

Report TVL, volume and users both with and without incentivised activity. If 80% disappears when incentives end, the honest number is the 20%, and investors will compute it whether you do or not.

Which vanity metrics should founders stop reporting?

Impressions and reach at the top of anything, follower counts as progress, waitlist size without a conversion rate, cumulative totals, incentivised volume without the unincentivised number, and partnerships announced without what each produced.

What is the difference between protocol fees and protocol revenue?

Fees are everything users pay to use a protocol. Revenue is the part the protocol keeps after paying liquidity providers and others. Incentives paid out in tokens should be netted against revenue.

Sources and notes

  • ANA, Media Rating Council updates viewable ad impression measurement guidelines, August 2015. Industry standard; a minimum exposure threshold, not a measure of attention.
  • Andreessen Horowitz, 16 Startup Metrics, 21 August 2015. Investor guidance; older, but the definitions are unchanged.
  • Keyrock, Airdrops in the Barren Desert, 25 September 2024. Research by a crypto market maker; 62 airdrops, price outcomes rather than user retention; the article gives both 88% and 85% for the decline share.
  • DefiLlama, Data definitions. Public analytics dashboard's own definitions; other dashboards define revenue differently.
  • The stage table, the audience table and the checklist are lowob's framework.
